author: NorthEast News Desk
body: McClatchy laid off more than 90 unionized journalists and media workers across 17 publications, according to the NewsGuild-CWA. The cuts represent about 30% of McClatchy employees represented by the union and affect papers including the Miami Herald, Sacramento Bee, Kansas City Star and Charlotte Observer.

The Miami Herald lost 32 positions, including 28 occupied jobs and four frozen posts, according to a person familiar with the changes cited by the Associated Press. The eliminated roles included the writing staff of Spanish-language El Nuevo Herald. The union also said the Charlotte Observer lost its two investigative reporters and that several local-government beats disappeared at other papers.

An internal McClatchy memo said the company could no longer maintain investment where subscriber interest did not support it. A company spokesperson did not respond to the AP’s request for comment. The reductions add to a broader wave of newsroom restructuring driven by declining print revenue, fragmented digital audiences and changing advertising markets.
dek: The layoffs span 17 publications and amount to about 30% of the chain’s NewsGuild-represented workforce.
headline: McClatchy cuts more than 90 unionized newsroom jobs
